items.prompt: A course that students must take is ___.
items.explanation: Compulsory means required.

items.prompt: She won a ___ that paid for her university fees.
items.explanation: A scholarship is money awarded to help pay for study.

items.prompt: The school introduced a new ___ with more science lessons.
items.explanation: A curriculum is the set of subjects taught in a school.

items.prompt: The company plans to ___ a new app next month.
items.explanation: We 'launch' a product or app.

items.prompt: Smartphones have become ___ in daily life; almost everyone uses one.
items.explanation: Ubiquitous means found everywhere.

items.prompt: A ___ is a mistake in a computer program.
items.explanation: A bug is an error in software.

items.prompt: Burning coal contributes to global ___.
items.explanation: 'Global warming' is the rise in Earth's temperature.

items.prompt: We must protect ___ species from disappearing.
items.explanation: Endangered species are at risk of dying out.

items.prompt: Wind and solar are examples of ___ energy.
items.explanation: Renewable energy comes from sources that do not run out.

items.prompt: A ___ diet includes fruit, vegetables and protein.
items.explanation: 'Balanced' is the adjective that fits before 'diet'.

items.prompt: Regular exercise can ___ the risk of heart disease.
items.explanation: We 'reduce' a risk (make it smaller).

items.prompt: Doctors advise people to avoid ___ lifestyles with too little movement.
items.explanation: A sedentary lifestyle involves a lot of sitting.

items.prompt: Employees who work from home enjoy more ___ in their schedules.
items.explanation: Flexibility means being able to adapt or change.

items.prompt: She was ___ to manager after five years.
items.explanation: To be promoted means to move to a higher position.

items.prompt: A person who starts and runs a business is an ___.
items.explanation: An entrepreneur creates and runs a business.

items.prompt: Many cities face ___, with too many people living in small areas.
items.explanation: Overcrowding means too many people in a space.

items.prompt: Volunteers make a valuable ___ to the community.
items.explanation: We 'make a contribution' to something.

items.prompt: The ___ between rich and poor has widened.
items.explanation: 'The gap between' two groups shows a difference.

items.prompt: We booked our flights and ___ months in advance.
items.explanation: Accommodation means a place to stay.

items.prompt: Tourism brings money, but it can also ___ local culture.
items.explanation: To damage means to harm.

items.prompt: A document that allows you to enter another country is a ___.
items.explanation: A visa gives permission to enter or stay in a country.

items.prompt: The ___ announced new taxes on sugary drinks.
items.explanation: The authorities are the people or bodies in charge.

items.prompt: Citizens over eighteen have the right to ___ in elections.
items.explanation: To vote is to choose in an election.

items.prompt: A new ___ will make it illegal to throw plastic into rivers.
items.explanation: A law is a rule made by a government.

items.prompt: Scientists carried out an ___ to test their theory.
items.explanation: An experiment is a test to discover or prove something.

items.prompt: The study's ___ were published in a journal.
items.explanation: Findings are the results of research.

items.prompt: A ___ is an idea that has not yet been proved.
items.explanation: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation to be tested.

items.prompt: Festivals help people preserve their cultural ___.
items.explanation: Heritage is traditions passed down over time.

items.prompt: Traditional music is ___ down from one generation to the next.
items.explanation: We 'pass down' traditions.

items.prompt: The museum has a large ___ of ancient pottery.
items.explanation: A collection is a group of items gathered together.

items.prompt: I ___ in this city since 2019.
items.explanation: 'Since' + a point in time needs the present perfect.

items.prompt: When I called, she ___ dinner.
items.explanation: Past continuous shows an action in progress when another happened.

items.prompt: By next June, I ___ my degree.
items.explanation: Future perfect: finished before a future time.

items.prompt: She is ___ honest person.
items.explanation: 'Honest' starts with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.

items.prompt: ___ sun rises in the east.
items.explanation: We use 'the' for unique things such as the sun.

items.prompt: He plays ___ guitar every evening.
items.explanation: We use 'the' with musical instruments.

items.prompt: She is good ___ mathematics.
items.explanation: 'Good at' is the correct collocation.

items.prompt: We arrived ___ the airport at noon.
items.explanation: We 'arrive at' a place like an airport.

items.prompt: He is interested ___ history.
items.explanation: 'Interested in' is correct.

items.prompt: The number of students ___ increasing.
items.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb.

items.prompt: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready.
items.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject (students).

items.prompt: Everyone ___ invited to the party.
items.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular.

items.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ at home.
items.explanation: First conditional: if + present, will + verb.

items.prompt: If she had studied harder, she ___ the exam.
items.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

items.prompt: I wish I ___ more time.
items.explanation: 'Wish' about the present uses the past simple.

items.prompt: The bridge ___ in 1990.
items.explanation: Passive past simple: was/were + past participle.

items.prompt: English ___ all over the world.
items.explanation: Passive present simple: is/are + past participle.

items.prompt: The results ___ next week.
items.explanation: Passive future: will be + past participle.

items.prompt: The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.
items.explanation: 'Who' refers to people as the subject.

items.prompt: That is the school ___ I studied.
items.explanation: 'Where' refers to a place.

items.prompt: He is the man ___ car was stolen.
items.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession.

items.prompt: You ___ wear a seatbelt; it is the law.
items.explanation: 'Must' expresses a strong obligation.

items.prompt: She ___ be at home; her light is on.
items.explanation: 'Must' also expresses a strong deduction.

items.prompt: He ___ swim when he was five.
items.explanation: 'Could' expresses ability in the past.

items.prompt: ___ it was raining, we went for a walk.
items.explanation: 'Although' shows contrast.

items.prompt: She stayed home ___ she felt ill.
items.explanation: 'Because' gives a reason.

items.prompt: I will call you ___ I arrive.
items.explanation: 'As soon as' links two actions in time.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Rarely do we see such talent.
Rarely we do see such talent.
We rarely do see such talent.
items.explanation: Negative adverbs at the start need inversion.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where lived I.
She asked me where I did live.
She asked me where did I live.
items.explanation: Reported questions use normal word order.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Not only is it cheap, but it is also durable.
Not only it is cheap, but also durable it is.
Not only is cheap it, but durable.
Not only it cheap is, but it durable is.
items.explanation: 'Not only' at the start needs inversion.
